newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico cement co's not paying higher U.S. duties.
newsitem.headline: Mexico cement co's not paying higher U.S. duties.

text.p: Mexican cement companies have to date not paid higher anti-dumping tariffs imposed by the United States earlier this year, industry officials said.
The U.S. Commerce Department raised tariffs on Mexican cement imports to 74.42 percent in April from 61.85 percent.

"We paid the 61.85 percent tariff during April and May, and it appears we will pay the same rate in June, so our second quarter results look good," Jaime Fernandez, spokesman for Grupo Cementos Chihuahua told Reuters.
An official at Cemex SA, the world's third biggest cement company, told Reuters they have also been paying the lower rate.

"When it becomes official, when they make it public in the U.S. customs centers, then the rate is paid," said the official, who asked to remain anonymous. Some industry analysts had feared cement companies second quarter results would be hurt by the higher tariffs, although companies like Cemex have diversified their exports from the U.S. market, which now only accounts for 20 percent of the company's exports.
